body:
This really looks like an issue with Bootstrap CSS, and should be fixed with CSS, not by editing our widgets. We chose Bootstrap because it was easy to use for our demo, but this should not have any influence on how we build our widgets.

> So `<div>` being unstyled by default will in the end by easier to use for most websites.

Don't think so. The easier for most websites will be to style a list like they already style lists. They could reuse the styles they have for `ul`/`li` and this will just work™. I even think most of them will already have a search page with a list of refinements (handled server-side) which will be rendered using `ul`/`li`.
